items.name: Power Profiles Daemon (PPD)
items.purpose: Selected power-policy backend; Noctalia exposes profile switching.
items.alternative: TuneD with tuned-ppd or TLP with tlp-pd, subject to pinned package/API support; neither is an automatic battery winner.
items.decision: Keep PPD as the measured baseline. Trial only one backend at a time with repeatable workload, energy and resume checks.

items.name: TLP, auto-cpufreq and TuneD candidates
items.purpose: Alternative policy paths, not selected: TLP and auto-cpufreq are explicitly disabled; TuneD is not declared.
items.alternative: Retain PPD; detailed AC/BAT policy or broader TuneD profiles only when a specific missing control warrants them.
items.decision: Availability means a candidate, not an installed binary. Check pinned options before replacing PPD; do not stack tuning daemons.

items.name: NVIDIA PRIME offload and RTD3
items.purpose: Razer hardware import supplies PRIME/runtime-PM defaults; local NVIDIA persistence is disabled and open beta driver selected.
items.alternative: A compatible stable driver or iGPU-only specialization; these can trade hardware support, CUDA and external outputs for simplicity.
items.decision: Verify inherited effective options and return to PCI runtime suspend after games, CUDA, displays and resume. Import presence is not a runtime result.

items.name: AMD P-state / EPP policy
items.purpose: Declares amd_pstate=active plus hardware-specific backlight parameters.
items.alternative: Firmware/platform profiles or another supported P-state mode after measurement, not extra governor scripts alongside PPD.
items.decision: Verify actual driver and supported profiles on the host; retain overrides only while their hardware benefit is reproducible.

items.name: Noctalia idle lock and suspend
items.purpose: Declares lock at 600 seconds, screen-off at 720 and lock-and-suspend at 1800; lockscreen enabled.
items.alternative: A separate idle manager only if the shell policy is insufficient; do not duplicate timers.
items.decision: Test lock-before-suspend and wake behavior. Fingerprint UI enablement does not prove fingerprint authentication is configured.

items.name: Hibernation / resume design
items.purpose: Potential disk-backed suspend; the declared 16G encrypted swapfile alone does not configure resume.
items.alternative: Keep ordinary suspend with encrypted overflow swap; zram cannot hold a power-off resume image.
items.decision: Defer until a resume device/offset strategy, memory sizing, NVIDIA behavior and recovery are tested; no hibernation guarantee.

items.name: Disko disk layout
items.purpose: Declares NVMe GPT, 1G EFI partition, encrypted Btrfs and tmpfs root; selected through the host's Disko import.
items.alternative: Hand-maintained filesystem declarations reduce installer automation but can drift from installation layout.
items.decision: Treat as a desired layout, not proof of existing partitions. Never execute formatting or installation commands as validation.

items.name: LUKS encrypted storage
items.purpose: Declares the crypted container for /nix, /saved and /swap; allows discards through encryption.
items.alternative: Disable discards for less allocation-pattern disclosure at an SSD-maintenance cost; TPM unlock is a separate proposal.
items.decision: Keep independent unlock credentials and header recovery. Verify on-disk metadata rather than inferring it from comments; /boot is outside this container.

items.name: Btrfs subvolumes and compression
items.purpose: Separate /nix, /saved and /swap subvolumes on one filesystem; zstd compression and noatime for store/persistent data.
items.alternative: Ext4 for simpler filesystem semantics; snapshots add local rollback convenience but are not off-device backup.
items.decision: Keep the layout unless evidence warrants migration; one physical device remains a shared failure domain.

items.name: Preservation and tmpfs root
items.purpose: Restores selected system/user state from /saved across ephemeral-root reboots; derives Flatpak state paths from the app list.
items.alternative: A persistent root or impermanence module changes state-management semantics rather than merely improving them.
items.decision: Audit every new stateful tool's paths. Downloads is not in the preserved user-directory list; persistence is neither backup nor secure deletion.

items.name: zram plus encrypted disk swap
items.purpose: Enables compressed RAM swap ahead of the disk swapfile declared in shadow/disk.nix.
items.alternative: Disk-only swap avoids compression CPU cost; RAM-only swap loses overflow capacity.
items.decision: Measure pressure and responsiveness before tuning sizes or algorithms; swap capacity does not establish hibernation.

items.name: Btrfs scrub and SMART monitoring
items.purpose: Monthly scrub via /saved covers the shared Btrfs filesystem; smartd is enabled for drive-health monitoring.
items.alternative: AC-gated scheduling and supported self-tests after hardware review; neither replaces backups.
items.decision: Verify timer execution, progress persistence and warning delivery. Checksums detect damage; repair needs a valid redundant copy.

items.name: Periodic SSD TRIM
items.purpose: Enables fstrim; the encrypted container permits discard pass-through.
items.alternative: Manual or AC-gated TRIM; disabling pass-through trades maintenance for less allocation leakage.
items.decision: Verify the effective timer and discard support. Keep maintenance separate from power-policy comparisons.

items.name: Independent encrypted backups (Restic / Borg)
items.purpose: Close the off-device recovery gap; no Restic/Borg job or repository is declared in the local Nix graph.
items.alternative: Restic or Borg according to destination, retention and recovery requirements; same-disk snapshots only supplement either.
items.decision: Inventory any existing external/manual backups first. Define coverage and independently recoverable keys, then prove an isolated restore before automation.

items.name: systemd-boot, systemd initrd and Plymouth
items.purpose: UEFI loader with eight-entry limit, systemd initrd and graphical unlock/progress prompt; latest kernel selected.
items.alternative: Compatible stable kernel or another loader only for demonstrated support/recovery needs; Plymouth is presentation, not boot integrity.
items.decision: Build and reboot-test each kernel/driver change. Eight boot entries do not guarantee eight retained generations after cleanup.

items.name: Lanzaboote / signed UKI Secure Boot
items.purpose: Possible authenticated boot chain; no Lanzaboote input/import or signing policy is locally declared.
items.alternative: Keep current systemd-boot/manual unlock with documented unsigned-boot risk until recovery and key handling are ready.
items.decision: Recovery first, then reviewed signing setup, persistent protected PKI, ESP headroom and firmware enrollment. UKI signing alone is not out-of-tree module signing.

items.name: TPM measured LUKS unlock
items.purpose: Optional measured-boot-bound unlock; no enrollment or PCR policy is declared.
items.alternative: Manual passphrase unlock is simpler and avoids accidental policy lockout; a PIN may complement a future TPM policy.
items.decision: Separate this from Secure Boot. Establish threat model, authenticated/measured artifacts, update policy and independent recovery before enrollment.

items.name: sudo-rs
items.purpose: Memory-safe privilege elevation selected instead of C sudo; preserves EDITOR and VISUAL.
items.alternative: C sudo may provide needed compatibility; language choice alone does not validate authorization policy.
items.decision: Keep sudoers changes under security.sudo-rs and test privileged workflows; do not enable both implementations.

items.name: USBGuard
items.purpose: USB allowlist for built-in keyboard controller, Bluetooth and camera; Aqua can use the IPC approval interface.
items.alternative: Unrestricted USB is convenient but removes this control; narrower rules require tested device identifiers.
items.decision: Test recovery input before changing rules. Approvals are security decisions; device ID/name matches are not cryptographic identity.

items.name: AppArmor coverage
items.purpose: Enables the LSM and available package profiles, but declares no blanket per-service confinement policy.
items.alternative: Targeted AppArmor profiles and systemd hardening can complement each other; enabling an LSM is not universal isolation.
items.decision: Inventory loaded enforcing profiles and actual process labels before claiming coverage; add policy only with reproduction and denial tests.

items.name: Kernel, journal and crash-data baseline
items.purpose: Memory initialization, IOMMU and sysctl hardening; security/baseline.nix disables coredumps and bounds persistent journal retention.
items.alternative: More restrictive ptrace/lockdown/module-signature settings can break debugging, Proton and unsigned NVIDIA/OpenRazer modules.
items.decision: Retain explicit tradeoffs; verify effective settings and avoid blanket hardening recipes that invalidate recovery or hardware support.

items.name: SOPS, age and sops-nix
items.purpose: Decrypts ciphertext for account hash, VPN import, Nix configuration and Noctalia template using a pre-provisioned persistent age identity.
items.alternative: Password/key managers or hardware-backed identities serve different consumers; GnuPG is also package-listed for manual encryption/signing.
items.decision: Back up the identity independently. Commit only ciphertext; never expose plaintext to the Nix store. CLI age/sops/gnupg come from home/packages/cli.nix.

items.name: secret ciphertext helper
items.purpose: Installs repository-specific list/status/edit/add/add-token wrapper with private plaintext input and no-clobber ciphertext publication.
items.alternative: Direct SOPS commands are more general but require careful format and output handling.
items.decision: Adding ciphertext is not deployment: declare and review its consumer separately. Keep plaintext sources outside the repository.

items.name: KeePassXC and GNOME Secrets
items.purpose: Package-installs KeePassXC, seeds writable private settings and browser bridge; GNOME Secrets is separately Flatpak-listed.
items.alternative: Choose one primary vault workflow; the GNOME login keyring is a Secret Service provider, not an automatic vault backup.
items.decision: Confirm Brave/native bridge pairing and vault location. This uses custom activation, not programs.keepassxc.settings; database recovery needs separate coverage.

items.name: fwupd / LVFS firmware updates
items.purpose: Enables firmware-update service while unused scanner, modem, online-account and iOS stacks are disabled.
items.alternative: Vendor firmware tools when supported devices are absent from LVFS; not all Razer/device firmware is available here.
items.decision: Inspect offered updates and recovery instructions; service enablement does not prove firmware currency or device support.

items.name: NetworkManager
items.purpose: Connection management, randomized Wi-Fi addressing and IPv6 temporary addresses; DNS handed to loopback rather than NM or resolved.
items.alternative: systemd-networkd/resolved suit other network models but would change DNS, GUI and VPN integration.
items.decision: Keep native connection management; verify inherited Wi-Fi backend, reconnect and captive-portal behavior rather than assuming defaults.

items.name: dnscrypt-proxy encrypted DNS
items.purpose: Loopback DNS cache with Cloudflare/Scaleway selection and DNSCrypt/DoH enabled; systemd-resolved disabled elsewhere.
items.alternative: Resolved encrypted DNS or another resolver may simplify integration, but protocol support, VPN DNS and bootstrap need comparison.
items.decision: Explicit server_names bypass require_* selection filters. Provider no-log claims are not an audit; test IPv4/IPv6, startup and VPN leaks.

items.name: Host firewall and local-only services
items.purpose: Enables the host firewall with no locally declared inbound allowances; Samba and Avahi are disabled in networkmanager.nix.
items.alternative: Narrow per-interface allowances only when a reviewed service actually needs LAN exposure.
items.decision: Inspect effective rules after all imports. Firewall enablement is not a substitute for loopback binding or application authentication.

items.name: WireGuard VPN import material
items.purpose: Provides root-only decrypted WireGuard configuration for manual NetworkManager import; does not declare an active VPN connection.
items.alternative: Declarative NetworkManager profile or native WireGuard service after DNS, route and credential review.
items.decision: Existing NM profiles remain authoritative. Verify connection, routes, DNS and leak behavior before claiming VPN coverage or a kill switch.

items.name: OpenSSH server
items.purpose: Server explicitly disabled; preservation conditionally retains host keys only if later enabled.
items.alternative: Keep no inbound SSH or enable a narrowly scoped key-only server when remote administration is required.
items.decision: This is not an installed/running-server claim. Enabling requires authentication, firewall and stable host-identity review.

items.name: curl, xh, dig and nmap
items.purpose: Package-listed HTTP, DNS and network diagnostics; curl is system-listed in core/packages.nix and http aliases to xh.
items.alternative: xh is convenient for interactive HTTP; curl remains suitable for scripts. DNS tests must distinguish local, VPN and upstream answers.
items.decision: No services or scan schedules are configured. Use nmap only on authorized targets; shell aliases do not preserve original CLI syntax.

items.name: Niri Wayland desktop
items.purpose: Enables Niri/default session and Wayland application hints; Home Manager installs module-owned KDL and brightnessctl.
items.alternative: GNOME/KDE or another compositor offers different integration and layout, not an automatic modernization.
items.decision: Validate effective KDL including Noctalia's generated include; test AMD rendering, external screens and session startup.

items.name: Noctalia shell and generated themes
items.purpose: Enables shell user service; links SOPS-rendered TOML and immutable SVG, with generated Niri/Ghostty/Helix themes.
items.alternative: Independent bar, launcher, locker and theme tools permit granular choices but add integration owners.
items.decision: Keep shell assets beside the module. Verify generated files, template secret access and lock behavior rather than treating TOML as runtime proof.

items.name: greetd / tuigreet and GNOME keyring
items.purpose: TTY login into niri-session, keyring PAM unlock and bounded greeter restarts; includes a nested systemd-user PAM bypass.
items.alternative: Another display manager may avoid the workaround but changes session/login integration.
items.decision: Retest the documented deadlock and recovery login before removing the bypass; its security/session effects deserve a separate review.

items.name: XDG portals and file/media sharing
items.purpose: Niri module integration and desktop preferences support portal-mediated app access; no explicit local portal backend selection is declared.
items.alternative: Targeted backend preferences if effective routing is wrong; broad filesystem access is not a safe substitute for broken portals.
items.decision: Inspect evaluated/inherited portal setup and test file chooser, screencast and browser/Flatpak camera paths. Do not infer success from installation.

items.name: PipeWire, WirePlumber and RTKit
items.purpose: Enables PipeWire with ALSA, 32-bit ALSA and PulseAudio compatibility plus RTKit; preservation retains WirePlumber/PipeWire user state.
items.alternative: PulseAudio-only would remove the unified media path; dedicated tools are useful diagnostics, not replacements by default.
items.decision: Verify effective session manager, audio, Bluetooth and portal capture; microphone/camera permissions remain per application.

items.name: GTK, dconf, fonts, XDG and GVfs
items.purpose: Selects themes, multilingual UI preferences, MIME handlers, bookmarks and user directories; system modules supply fonts, keyring and GVfs.
items.alternative: Toolkit defaults simplify theming but may weaken cross-app consistency and multilingual rendering.
items.decision: Review MIME references against actual app declarations. Read-only bindfs font/icon projection for Flatpak lives in desktop/flatpak-theming.nix.

items.name: nix-flatpak and sandbox policy
items.purpose: Installs declared apps, daily updates, unmanaged-app cleanup and replacement system overrides; verified/default/full/beta remote choices are explicit.
items.alternative: Native Nix packages avoid a second update plane but do not automatically provide Flatpak-style confinement.
items.decision: Review per-app manifest plus system/user overrides; global denials do not erase every specific grant. Flatpak versions are not pinned by flake.lock.

items.name: Native GNOME utility applications
items.purpose: System package list: Nautilus, Text Editor, Loupe, Showtime, Papers, Resources, Disks and Calendar; no individual programs.* settings.
items.alternative: Selected Flatpak equivalents or other toolkit apps where sandbox or feature requirements justify them.
items.decision: Keep package installation distinct from settings/MIME management in Home Manager; Showtime and Flatpak Cine coexist, with Cine selected for media MIME types.

items.name: Obsidian, Mullvad Browser, Anki and Stremio
items.purpose: Home package list installs standalone apps plus wl-screenrec; these entries are not dedicated program/service modules.
items.alternative: SiYuan and Zotero are separately Flatpak-declared; browser isolation choices do not establish a VPN.
items.decision: Check each app's persistent data and actual use. Anki and Obsidian paths are preserved; app install alone does not manage content or accounts.

items.name: Brave Origin browser
items.purpose: Managed through programs.chromium with Brave package, extensions, Wayland/video flags and AMD render-node override.
items.alternative: Mullvad Browser is package-listed for another privacy workflow; Firefox-family choices require separate settings and extension review.
items.decision: Verify render-node identity and hardware decoding; ignore-gpu-blocklist is an explicit tradeoff, not proof of safe acceleration.

items.name: Flatpak productivity, reading and communication suite
items.purpose: Declares LibreOffice, Planify, Foliate, PDF Arranger, Zotero, SiYuan, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Element, Tuba, NewsFlash, Tsukimi and Reflection.
items.alternative: Native packages or fewer overlapping apps can simplify upkeep; full/beta remote apps need a separate trust decision from verified-subset apps.
items.decision: App IDs are the install/override/persistence source of truth; reviewed membership does not prove login, usability or sandbox behavior.

items.name: Flatpak media and specialist utilities
items.purpose: Declares Cine, Archives, Ear Tag, Nocturne, Upscaler, Video Trimmer, Subtitle Composer, Raider and Impression, with selected strict/offline exceptions.
items.alternative: Native FFmpeg and ouch suit scripted jobs; GUI conveniences and device-access tools have different permission needs.
items.decision: Test file grants and offline restrictions. Impression's broad device access is intentional and deserves caution; GNOME Secrets is cataloged with password managers.

items.name: Steam, Proton GE, GameMode and Prism Launcher
items.purpose: Enables Steam/protontricks/GameMode, 32-bit graphics and XWayland; Flatpak Prism declares NVIDIA offload and X11 hints.
items.alternative: Native Wayland where games support it, or other launchers for a specific library; compatibility remains game-dependent.
items.decision: Test offload return-to-idle and actual Flatpak X11 permissions: global !x11/!fallback-x11 policy may conflict with Prism's intent.

items.name: AppImage and browser desktop launchers
items.purpose: Declares NahhasCinema launcher pointing to /saved/apps/NahhasCinema.AppImage; system AppImage binfmt enabled. Web-app module adds WhatsApp/Rust Book entries.
items.alternative: A packaged app gives reproducible provenance; browser apps avoid maintaining another native wrapper.
items.decision: Launcher declarations do not fetch the local AppImage or install a Brave WhatsApp profile app. Check file provenance, executable presence and browser app registration.

items.name: Kavita local book server
items.purpose: Declares loopback-only port 8083, private persisted data and read-only Books binding with systemd hardening.
items.alternative: Foliate for local reading or another library service if actual features warrant it.
items.decision: wantedBy is explicitly empty: configured for manual start, not autostart/running. Review library access and token-key persistence before use.

items.name: Bluetooth and OpenRazer / Polychromatic
items.purpose: Imports Bluetooth enabled but not powered on at boot, OpenRazer access and package-listed Polychromatic.
items.alternative: Firmware defaults or narrower peripheral tools reduce extra kernel/service surface if features are unused.
items.decision: Verify USBGuard permits required devices and test resume. OpenRazer's out-of-tree module matters to future signing/lockdown decisions.

items.name: Fish, Starship, Atuin, fzf and zoxide
items.purpose: Managed interactive shell, prompt, history, fuzzy selection and navigation; Atuin owns Ctrl-R and system users select Fish.
items.alternative: Bash/Zsh for different compatibility; external history synchronization requires a separate privacy/credential decision.
items.decision: Interactive aliases are not POSIX command replacements. Preserve history intentionally; this declaration does not prove a remote Atuin account/sync setup.

items.name: eza, bat, fd, ripgrep, dust, duf, procs and btop
items.purpose: Package-list modern inspection tools plus chafa, fastfetch, FFmpeg, ouch, zip and unzip for media/archives; aliases are owned by Fish modules. zip also serves Noctalia's office theme.
items.alternative: Coreutils/findutils/procps remain better compatibility targets for many scripts; newer UI does not imply identical flags/output.
items.decision: Use explicit binaries in scripts and documentation when semantics matter; Fastfetch display is information, not an audit guarantee.

items.name: Ghostty terminal
items.purpose: Program module manages font, keys, clipboard behavior, Fish integration and generated Noctalia theme.
items.alternative: Foot, Kitty or another terminal according to accessibility, rendering and workflow needs.
items.decision: Test theme bootstrap, clipboard and font fallback; avoid changing a working terminal merely because another is newer.

items.name: Helix and Zed editors
items.purpose: Managed Zed FHS wrapper, settings/extensions/LSP plus AMD-only Vulkan visibility; Helix is separately managed and selected as EDITOR.
items.alternative: VS Code/Neovim or project-local tools when extensions/workflows require them; no universal editor winner.
items.decision: Keep editor preferences separate from compiler/toolchain declarations. VISUAL uses zeditor --wait; test language tools through trusted project environments.

items.name: nixd, nixfmt, statix and deadnix
items.purpose: Package-list Nix language server, formatter and linters; Zed wires nixd/nixfmt, and flake.nix supplies the repository formatter.
items.alternative: nil or other lint/format choices if a concrete gap exists; lint suggestions are not automatically safe module edits.
items.decision: Use formatting/linting deliberately. Project Rust/C++/JS compiler and LSP settings do not prove global toolchain installation.

items.name: devenv, direnv and nix-direnv
items.purpose: Enables direnv/nix-direnv; development package list adds devenv and Zed loads direnv directly.
items.alternative: Plain flake devShells minimize extra workflow machinery; devenv adds project environment/service conventions.
items.decision: No root devShell is declared in this flake. Review .envrc before allowing execution and use project-local toolchains rather than global language bundles.

items.name: Git, gh and lazygit
items.purpose: Home package list installs forge CLI and Git TUI; Git is system-listed and its user configuration/gh state are preserved.
items.alternative: Direct Git or a graphical forge workflow for different interaction needs; gh implies no configured login.
items.decision: Keep credential state private and separate CLI installation from authentication, signing and repository permissions.

items.name: Codex, OpenCode, ACP and ChatGPT desktop
items.purpose: Enables CLI agents/persona and Zed custom ACP adapters; desktop/chatgpt.nix enables the community-packaged ChatGPT/Codex GUI.
items.alternative: Built-in Zed provider, another remote provider or the parked local stack; compare privacy, cost and tool permissions, not only model claims.
items.decision: Provider login is runtime state. Keep Codex config writable for the GUI, review third-party wrapper/input updates, and do not assume sandbox settings cover every external agent.

items.name: Parked llama.cpp CUDA / llama-swap stack
items.purpose: Existing unimported module describes local model router, manual ai function, model directory and Zed endpoint; parent import is commented out.
items.alternative: Retain remote agents or reconsider a CPU/backend/model combination with acceptable quality, energy and build costs.
items.decision: Not configured in the active graph. Re-import and restore launcher together only after CUDA build cost, model provenance, VRAM and endpoint permissions are reviewed.

items.name: Zed Delta application
items.purpose: Home package list selects the delta-nix flake application; AI module supplies its instruction file and preservation retains state.
items.alternative: Existing Zed/Codex/OpenCode workflows may avoid another overlapping application.
items.decision: This is the Zed Delta input/package, not git-delta diff pagination. Audit external input trust and actual credentials/tool permissions separately.

items.name: Zed agent sandbox and language-tool downloads
items.purpose: Declares native-agent host allowlist and disallows unsandboxed operation; development.nix comments out bubblewrap/socat and Biome requires project config.
items.alternative: Verified project-local binaries and narrower permissions reduce downloaded execution; FHS/bubblewrap packaging alone does not prove agent confinement.
items.decision: Verify the installed Zed sandbox support, failures and external-agent boundary. Private-file globs are not a comprehensive data-loss prevention policy.

items.name: Flakes, binary caches, nh and garbage collection
items.purpose: Enables flakes/Nix commands, root-only daemon trust, declared cache keys, Friday optimization and nh cleanup retaining minimum generations/age.
items.alternative: Manual maintenance or narrower named-input updates offer more control at an operator-time cost.
items.decision: Review flake.lock diffs and cache trust; keep a known-good generation. Boot-entry limits and cleanup retention are distinct; never bump stateVersion simply to update.

items.name: Gitleaks, flake checks and no-link builds
items.purpose: Declares Gitleaks flake check and nixfmt/fd formatter; repository workflow requires flake evaluation, diff checks and full-system no-link build.
items.alternative: Targeted evaluation is quicker feedback but cannot replace full integration/build and reboot tests for hardware changes.
items.decision: A check declaration is not a passing result. Use nh os test only for reviewed system changes; this catalog does not authorize switching or Disko operations.
